th-1016-1.text:
Nerves before a fight don't mean you're not ready.

They mean your body knows it matters.

The fighters who look calm aren't fearless. They just stopped reading fear as a stop sign.

th-1016-2.text:
Honest question for the fighters here.

What's the round you dread most in training?

First round cold, the middle grind, or the last one when everything's gone?

th-1016-3.text:
No coach? Film every session.

You can't fix what you can't see. Watch it the same day, pick one thing, fix only that this week.

One fix a week is 52 fixes a year.

th-1017-1.text:
Discipline isn't motivation.

It's kept promises.

Pick one thing you do every single day. Keep it for 30 days. That's where the mindset actually comes from.

th-1017-2.text:
Which one is you?

1. You train when no fight is booked
2. You keep going after getting dropped in sparring
3. You've never needed a crowd to show up

Drop the number.

th-1017-3.text:
The sparring session you lose to someone better is worth more than ten you win.

Getting picked apart shows you every hole at once.

Watch it back the same night. Every mistake is right there.

th-1018-1.text:
You're mentally tougher than you think if you've lost and come back the next day.

Not the next week. The next day.

That's the whole test.

th-1018-2.text:
What do you say in your head when you get hit clean?

One word beats a speech. Something like: reset.

What's yours?

th-1018-3.text: How to stay calm in a fight when you don't have years of experience. A thread.

th-1019-1.text:
A bad session ruining your whole day isn't weakness.

It means you care more than most people in the gym.

Just don't let it ruin tomorrow's session too.

th-1019-2.text:
Rest days.

Do they feel like recovery or like punishment?

Be honest.

th-1019-3.text:
You don't need weights to hit harder.

Turn the back foot. Relax until impact. Exhale sharp on every shot.

Power starts on the floor. No pivot, no punch.
